images.title: Which blog platform fits your goal
images.alt: Decision chart matching blog goals to platforms: self-hosted WordPress for ads and affiliates, Ghost or Substack for paid readers, a free option to test.
images.caption: Pick by who handles the upkeep and how freely you can earn, not by features.

data.question: What is the blog mainly for?

branches.result: Self-hosted WordPress, or a paid WordPress.com plan if you don't want a server.
Ghost, or Substack if you want zero setup.
Start on a free option and move later. Moving a site is real work.

images.after: Step 4: Set up the few pages and settings that matter
images.title: Finish these before your first article
images.alt: Checklist of blog setup essentials: About and Contact pages, privacy policy, affiliate disclosure, HTTPS, readable theme, Search Console, email signup.
images.caption: Skip logo design, custom fonts and plugin shopping for now.

items: About page that says who writes the blog and why to trust it
Contact page or a visible email address
Privacy policy, before analytics, ads or an email form
Affiliate disclosure, if you'll use affiliate links
HTTPS on, and clean URLs that use the post name
Search Console with your sitemap, plus analytics and email signup

images.title: Four ways a blog earns
images.alt: Four blog income methods: display ads, affiliate links, your own products such as ebooks or courses, and services like freelancing or coaching.
images.caption: Most blogs that last use more than one, and results vary widely.

items.title: Display ads
items.text: Pay per visit, but the amount is small, so they need a lot of traffic.

items.title: Affiliate links
items.text: A commission on purchases. Best on comparisons and reviews.

items.title: Your own products
items.text: Ebooks, templates or courses. Keep more per sale, but take time to make.

items.title: Services
items.text: Freelance work, consulting or coaching. Often a blog's first income.
